sig_title_tooltip: Empty: the default title in the language of the user
sig_maxCurrent_tooltip: Upper limit of the slider; the rated current of the charger caps it in addition. 0 = rated current only
micro_device_none: No SigenMicro found — enable the cloud in the sigenergy adapter
charging_running_hint: Charging in progress — press stop to end it
ac_tip_0: System init (0): the charger is starting up and has no valid state yet.
ac_tip_1: A1/A2 (1): no vehicle connected, the plug is free. A1 = charger not ready, A2 = charger ready and waiting for a vehicle.
ac_tip_2: B1 (2): vehicle plugged in, the charger has not released charging yet (e.g. app/backend, load management, lock).
ac_tip_3: B2 (3): vehicle plugged in and charging released, but the vehicle does not request power (yet) — e.g. battery full, charging schedule in the car, charging pause.
ac_tip_4: C1 (4): the vehicle requests charging, the charger gives no release / no PWM — a transition, e.g. while charging ends or when charging is locked.
ac_tip_5: C2 (5): charging — the vehicle requests power, the charger releases it and energy flows.
ac_tip_6: F (6): charger not available or fault of the charging station — e.g. internal fault, overtemperature, shutdown by load management.
ac_tip_7: E (7): fault of the pilot signal / charging cable — short circuit or interruption of the CP signal, power failure, cable or vehicle fault.
ac_tip_none: No value received for the system state.
dc_tip_0: Idle (0): no vehicle connected, the charger is ready and waiting.
dc_tip_1: Occupied (1): the connector is plugged into the vehicle, but there is no connection or detection yet — the handshake has not started.
dc_tip_2: Preparing (2): establishing communication with the vehicle — negotiation per CCS/ISO 15118 or DIN 70121 (charging parameters, voltage and current limits).
dc_tip_3: Charging (3): charging in progress, direct current is delivered to the vehicle.
dc_tip_4: Fault (4): charging aborted or blocked by a fault (e.g. insulation fault, overtemperature, communication loss). The charger only charges again once the fault is acknowledged or cleared.
dc_tip_5: Scheduled (5): scheduled charging — vehicle connected, charging is deferred by a time or charging plan and starts at the planned time.
dc_tip_6: Ended (6): charging ended — the session is complete (battery full, stopped by user/vehicle or target reached); the connector is usually still plugged in.
dc_tip_7: Unavailable (7): the charger is out of service, e.g. maintenance mode, locked or disabled by the system.
dc_tip_8: Discharging (8): bidirectional operation (V2H/V2G) — energy flows from the vehicle battery back into the house or grid.
dc_tip_9: Alarm (9): a warning is present that does not necessarily abort charging (unlike fault). See the alarm registers for details.
dc_tip_10: Preparing (10): insulation check — before high voltage is released, the insulation resistance of the DC line to the vehicle is checked (safety step right before charging starts).
dc_tip_pwr_charging: Charging — the output power is greater than 0.
dc_tip_pwr_discharging: Discharging — the output power is negative (V2H/V2G).
dc_hint_no_state_oid: The state is derived from the output power only, because no state object ID (dcCharger.runningState) is set in the widget settings.
dc_hint_power_only: The state is derived from the output power only.
dc_hint_old_protocol: The running state of the charger (register 31513) is only delivered from Sigenergy protocol V2.8; the device reports %s.
dc_hint_no_value: The adapter delivers no value for %s although the device reports protocol %s. Either the charger marks the register as not valid, or the adapter sorted it out as not supported — the adapter log shows under the block 31509–31518 which of the two applies.
dc_hint_no_protocol: The adapter delivers no value for %s (running state of the charger, needs Sigenergy protocol V2.8). The protocol version of the instance cannot be read here — set the object ID "Protocol version" (info.protocolVersion) in the widget settings, then this hint names the concrete reason.
dc_hint_invalid: The charger reports the value "not valid" (0xFFFF) for register 31513 and so provides no running state. This is neither an adapter nor a configuration problem — the other DC charger registers (rated power, PV yield, meters) are read normally. Adapters from 3.3.1 deliver no value for such registers instead of passing the raw 65535 through.
sm_cloud_lost: Cloud connection lost — values may be outdated
sm_no_device: No micro-inverter selected — choose them in the widget settings or press "Take all SigenMicro".
